title: How a prescription carries the practitioner's 'no substitution' instruction under 105 CMR 721.020(B)
rule_summary: 105 CMR 721.020(B) provides that a Prescription must enable the practitioner to instruct the pharmacist to dispense a brand name Drug Product by indicating 'no substitution', provided that (1) the indication of 'no substitution' is not the default indication; (2) the Prescription indicates that 'Interchange is mandated unless the practitioner indicates "no substitution" in accordance with the law'; and (3) the indication of 'no substitution' is a unique element in the Prescription and shall not be satisfied by use of any other element, including the signature. 105 CMR 721.010 defines a Prescription as an oral, written or electronic order for a medication or device which is dispensed to or for an ultimate user, not including an order for medication which is dispensed for immediate administration to the ultimate user, and a Drug Product as the final dosage form of a drug that is marketed under a brand or generic name. Under 105 CMR 721.003 the standards in 105 CMR 721.000 are the standards for format and security that all Prescriptions issued by practitioners or reduced to writing by pharmacists must meet in order to comply with M.G.L. c. 112, § 12D and M.G.L. c. 94C.
exam_relevance: Tests that the practitioner's signature does not supply the 'no substitution' indication, that the indication may not be a default, and that the prescription itself carries the statement that interchange is mandated unless 'no substitution' is indicated.

authority.name: Standards for Prescription Format and Security in Massachusetts
authority.section: 105 CMR 721.020(B), with 105 CMR 721.003 and the definitions in 105 CMR 721.010

common_confusions: Treating the practitioner's signature as the 'no substitution' instruction. The indication is a unique element that no other element, including the signature, satisfies.
Accepting a pre-selected 'no substitution' setting. The indication shall not be the default indication.
Looking for a handwriting requirement. 105 CMR 721.020(B) states the three conditions above and does not require the indication to be handwritten.
verification_notes: Read in the current 105 CMR 721.000 published on mass.gov (page footers dated 9/27/24) on 2026-09-16, including 721.003 and the definitions in 721.010.
